task_objective: Explain the exposure from default router administrator credentials and replace them with a strong unique administrator secret.

rius.description: Explain that a default administrator password may be known or easily discovered and can let someone who reaches the administration interface take control of router settings.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Explain that a default administrator password may be known or easily discovered and can let someone who reaches the administration interface take control of router settings.

rius.rationale: Without the default-credential-to-administrative-access link the requested explanation of the risk is absent; internet exposure is not assumed.

rius.description: Replace the default router administrator password with a strong unique password or equivalently secure supported administrator credential.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Replace the default router administrator password with a strong unique password or equivalently secure supported administrator credential.

rius.rationale: Leaving default administrative credentials intact leaves the stated exposure unresolved even if other router settings are improved.

notes: E6 draft; frozen prompt corpus v0.3.1, protocol 0.3, annotation schema 0.2. EN/BN/BN-CS interpretation: All variants specify the default administrator password of a home router, not merely its wireless-network password. The Bengali plural change wording does not introduce additional mandatory router-hardening tasks. Boundaries: The access-risk explanation and administrator-credential change are distinct. No compulsory Wi-Fi password change, firmware upgrade, router replacement or particular password manager. A changed wireless password alone does not fulfill the administrator change. Equivalent wording, scripts and numerals are accepted. Defeating contradictions override positive anchors; a refusal/non-answer scores 0 on every RIU. CHECK-01 is separate and can flag the same span as an RIU error.
